title: Someone else's task is not yours — it is a monitor
setup: party model; sp_goa_dec; the roster resolves "karan" to contact:karan. Shipped rule (decide.v9 rule 3 + brain/decide-pass.ts applyTask): a task whose owner is not the user is stored as THEIRS, forced to advise-only, and filed as a monitor for the user (`create_monitor`) — the user's own list gains nothing.
input_events: "karan book YOUR ticket, rest of us are done".
expected: No task lands in ADITYA's list. The ticket is Karan's: the answer may carry it with owner = the Karan roster ref, and the task writer then stores it as Karan's, forces advise-only and files the monitoring item ("Karan's ticket pending") on the space — that is the monitor the rubric asks for, and it is what `applied_by_task_writer` shows. What must never appear is a task the USER owns.

wrong.label: task-theft
wrong.assert_absent: a task owned by the user (self / user / me / no owner) telling Aditya to book Karan's ticket — the user's own list gaining an item that is not the user's

wrong.label: silent-drop
wrong.assert_absent: Karan's pending ticket dropped entirely — neither a task of his nor a monitor for the user

source.section: TSK-04 · Someone else's task is not yours (re-authored V6 P1 R3 — the V1 wording read as "emit no task at all", but the shipped shape is a task owned by the other person that the writer turns into a monitor for the user, which DEC-05 asserts as code; the assertion is unchanged, the vocabulary is the product's)
